summary.headline: EID Parry Q2 FY27: sugar realisation rose to Rs 45.11/kg and sugar revenue to Rs 486 crore, while management flags a ~10% smaller cane crop next year.
summary.overview: Sugar performance improved YoY on higher volume (84,000 t sold vs 73,000 t) and higher realisation (Rs 45.11/kg vs Rs 40.67/kg), lifting sugar revenue to about Rs 486 crore from Rs 368 crore. Distillery volumes and realisation fell YoY, with alcohol realisation at Rs 63.99/litre vs Rs 67.55/litre. The consumer products segment turnover fell to about Rs 120 crore from Rs 165 crore as low-margin lines were exited, and management is targeting break-even in FY28. Management expects a shorter 2627 crushing season with a roughly 10% lower cane crop next year, and India may need to import sugar. Management gave no formal guidance; it said the full-year outlook is better than last year but would be formalised with Q3 results.

financial_highlights.value: 385 lakh units generated; 175 lakh units exported
financial_highlights.change: vs 307 lakh and 128 lakh units YoY

segments.name: Sugar
segments.commentary: Crushed 4.03 lakh t (vs 3.66 lakh t) over 66 days (vs 48); recovery 7.86% (vs 7.97%); sugar produced 32,000 t (vs 27,000 t); closing stock about 56,000 t; cane landed cost about Rs 3,798/t (vs Rs 3,720/t).

segments.name: Distillery / alcohol
segments.commentary: Production 307 lakh litres (vs 392 lakh litres); sales 440 lakh litres including ENA 212 lakh and ethanol 234 lakh litres. Average realisation fell to Rs 63.99/litre from Rs 67.55/litre.

segments.name: Cogeneration
segments.commentary: Generation 385 lakh units (vs 307 lakh); exports 175 lakh units (vs 128 lakh); tariff Rs 3.73/unit vs Rs 4.04/unit; revenue about Rs 17.67 crore vs Rs 11.94 crore.

segments.name: Consumer products (CPG)
segments.commentary: Turnover about Rs 120 crore vs Rs 165 crore on lower bulk and low-margin sales; management said margins improved QoQ on higher realisation and a shift to high-margin products. Target break-even in FY28; the segment is in opex investment mode, not capex.

segments.name: Nutraceuticals (US subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Management described H1 FY27 as stronger than last year, led by joint health and greens/immunity, with new derm and hair-care launches from palmetto berry extract. Revenue was not given in the call.

segments.name: Refinery (PSRIPL)
segments.commentary: Operations ceased; all inventories sold by 30 September. In-principle exit letter received in April; duty workings submitted in June, with final duty payment expected in Q3. Asset monetisation to start after FESF and environmental clearance.

guidance_outlook: Full-year FY27 (sugar, distillery and cogen combined) expected to be better than last year; no quantified guidance, to be revisited with Q3 results.
Ethanol production for the current year (sugar year 2526 season) estimated at 14 to 15 crore litres, with some volume shifting to ENA/EMA.

Consumer products: break-even targeted in FY28; FY27 consumer revenue expected to reach about Rs 500 crore, with 20-25% growth next year (as stated in a media interview and referenced by an analyst; not confirmed on the call).
Karnataka crushing season expected to be 10 to 15 days shorter; management's estimate for next year's cane crop is about 10% lower.
Sugar-year 2627 India likely to need sugar imports.
capex_capacity: No new capex or inorganic capacity planned in sugar or biofuel; focus on running existing operations.
No capital allocation planned for nutraceuticals; consumer business needs opex, not capex.
Refinery asset divestment under way; proceeds intended to strengthen the standalone balance sheet, with future capital allocation to the food/FMCG segment.
Substrate (green-road media) commercialisation in progress; biochemical opportunities not being pursued now.
demand_pricing: Global: sugar market moving from 1.1 mt surplus in 2526 to 0.2 mt deficit in 2627; white sugar rose from about $467/t (July) to $518/t (September); raw sugar rose from 14.8 to 17.9 c/lb.

India: poor southwest monsoon, lower inventories and seasonal demand raised prices in Q2; government actions (duty-free raw sugar imports, tighter dealer stock limits, more frequent quota releases) eased prices by quarter-end.
India 2526 balance sheet: production 31 mt, ethanol diversion 3.1 mt, domestic consumption 28.5 mt, exports 0.8 mt, closing stock 3.7 mt.
Sugarcane price in north Karnataka is around Rs 3,800/t, versus FRP of about Rs 3,300-3,400/t; formula still being negotiated under a government expert committee.
Institutional sugar contracts: most long-term contracts shifted to tender; contracts now around 15-24 days, with prices mirroring spot.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of the uneven monsoon on Karnataka and Maharashtra cane and next year's sugar output?
qa_highlights.answer: Karnataka crushing season estimated 10-15 days shorter, versus 8-10 days lost so far, driven by water availability. Next year's cane crop could be about 10% lower, with sugarcane yield down 8-10% in some estimates.

qa_highlights.question: Sugarcane price formula and the farmer profit-sharing arrangement?
qa_highlights.answer: The formula agreed two weeks ago may no longer apply after farmer agitation. Mills in north Karnataka are paying around Rs 3,800/t against FRP of about Rs 3,300-3,400/t. A binding framework is awaited.

qa_highlights.question: Ethanol volumes this year, given the lack of B-heavy and juice and feedstock fungibility?
qa_highlights.answer: Current-year ethanol could be 14-15 crore litres. Some volume may shift to ENA/EMA, and the government allocation formula is 35-40% of base ethanol. Next year's volume will depend on how things evolve.

qa_highlights.question: Tamil Nadu margins versus Karnataka, and whether the full year will beat last year?
qa_highlights.answer: Tamil Nadu cane volumes are 8-10% higher this year, but cost of production is higher, so it will not materially change company margins. The full year is expected to be better than last year, with formal guidance deferred to Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Consumer products outlook, capital needs and non-core asset monetisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Break-even targeted in FY28; investment is opex-led (brand, distribution, product development). Contribution margin has moved up. Refinery asset divestment is progressing, with proceeds for the standalone balance sheet. No buyback discussion.

qa_highlights.question: Nutraceuticals three verticals and growth drivers; biochemical or biofuel expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Three verticals: greens/immunity (spirulina, tremella), joint health (human and pet), and palmetto-based prostate and derm/hair health. Recent growth is from pet joint health and derm launches. No biochemical expansion; only substrate work.

risks_watch: Sugarcane availability next year: a potential 10% drop in cane supply, with a shorter Karnataka season.
Sugarcane pricing policy in Karnataka and Maharashtra remains unsettled; the expert committee outcome and any binding formula are pending.
Ethanol allocation and feedstock shift toward ENA/EMA could cap distillery volumes.
Consumer products breakeven by FY28 depends on distribution expansion and new launches; revenue fell 27% YoY in Q2.
Final refinery duty payment expected in Q3; asset monetisation depends on FESF and environmental clearance.
Sugar price volatility given short-tenor contracts; government intervention (import, stock limits, quotas) could affect realisations.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the sugar cycle and the sugar realisation improvement, but cautious and non-committal on full-year guidance, cane pricing in Karnataka, and ethanol allocation, which management said remain unsettled. Management was more forthright about the consumer and nutraceutical turnaround plans.

growth.why: No formal quantified guidance; management says FY27 full-year outlook is better than last year, to be formalised with Q3 results, with no new capex or inorganic capacity in sugar or biofuel, and the Q2 gain rests on higher sugar volume and realisation (84,000 t vs 73,000 t; Rs 45.11/kg vs Rs 40.67/kg) while the CPG segment is targeted to break even in FY28.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Sugar realisation rose to Rs 45.11/kg from Rs 40.67/kg, but cane landed cost rose to about Rs 3,798/t from Rs 3,720/t and distillery realisation fell to Rs 63.99/litre from Rs 67.55/litre, so margin gains are not assured.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Management said no new capex or inorganic capacity is planned in sugar or biofuel, and the focus is on running existing operations.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Sugar volume rose to 84,000 t from 73,000 t and alcohol sales to 440 lakh litres from 409 lakh, but next year's Karnataka cane crop could be about 10% lower with a 10-15 day shorter season.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation was not disclosed, and management said no new sugar or biofuel capex is planned; refinery divestment proceeds are meant to strengthen the balance sheet.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management said full-year FY27 should be better than last year but gave no quantified guidance, with formal numbers deferred to Q3 results.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Cane supply for next year could fall about 10%, Karnataka cane pricing (about Rs 3,800/t vs FRP Rs 3,300-3,400/t) is unsettled, and ethanol allocation may cap distillery volumes.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Nutraceuticals are launching derm and hair-care products from palmetto berry extract, and the consumer business is targeting break-even in FY28 with opex-led brand and distribution investment.

rows.label: Consumer products break-even in FY28
rows.why: CPG turnover fell to about Rs 120 crore from Rs 165 crore as low-margin lines were exited, but margins improved QoQ and management targets break-even in FY28.

rows.label: Refinery final duty payment and asset monetisation
rows.why: In-principle exit letter received in April and duty workings submitted in June, with final duty payment expected in Q3; monetisation starts only after FESF and environmental clearance.

rows.label: India sugar imports in 2627
rows.why: Management said India is likely to need sugar imports in sugar year 2627, and global balance is moving from a 1.1 mt surplus to a 0.2 mt deficit.

tone.note: Management was confident on the sugar cycle and realisation gains but cautious on full-year guidance, Karnataka cane pricing and ethanol allocation; analysts pressed on cane supply, pricing formula and ethanol volumes.

quality.why: Sugar revenue rose about 32% (Rs 368 cr to Rs 486 cr) from both higher volume (84,000 t vs 73,000 t, about +15%) and higher realisation (Rs 45.11/kg vs Rs 40.67/kg, about +11%), with the price lift driven by a tight global and domestic market, but the brief flags no one-off items; the consumer products segment fell about 27% and distillery realisation dropped, which tempers the overall growth.
